why: Daniel breaks dictated points out as bullets in the middle of prose (fill2-note-193 action items: lead-in line ending in a colon, '- ' bullets, prose resumes after).
behaviour: partway through, after some normal prose, the speaker announces a set of three to five points and dictates them in a run ("so there are a few things I need from you, first the signed contract, second...", "my main points are, one... two...", "a couple of things, the deck, and also the budget sheet, and then..."), each point a short phrase or a sentence, then goes back to normal prose and signs off
rule: Break a run of three or more dictated points out as a bulleted list in the middle of the text: the lead-in on its own line ending in a colon ("A few things I need from you:"), then one '- ' bullet per point, capitalised, without the spoken ordinals or joiners (first, second, number one, and also, and then), keeping every detail of each point; resume the prose as a new paragraph after the list. Keep the prose before and after as paragraphs. Two short items inside one sentence stay in the sentence.
